subtopic: Scope limits of single-paper quantization claims
learningObjective: Recognise the scope limits and common overclaims around single-paper quantization results (SmoothQuant, GPTQ, AWQ).
stem: A colleague summarizes recent quantization work by combining results from SmoothQuant, GPTQ and AWQ into universal claims. Which THREE of the following statements about interpreting these papers are correct?

options.text: The papers' accuracy results are conditioned on specific model families, sizes, tasks and calibration sets; extending them to 'LLMs in general' (including smaller models, code/math tasks and long-tail benchmarks) requires additional evaluation.

Reported wall-clock speedups depend on the availability of an efficient dequantized-GEMM kernel for the given precision/granularity on the target hardware; the same scheme can be faster on one GPU generation and no faster (or slower) on another.

An ablation study (e.g. SmoothQuant's migration-factor α) supports the specific mechanism it isolates but does not by itself establish head-to-head superiority over other quantization methods at every setting.

Because all three papers report memory footprint reductions when quantizing to 4-bit, one can conclude that 4-bit quantization always yields ≥3× end-to-end latency speedup regardless of hardware and kernel implementation.

explanation: A, B, C reflect careful reading of the papers' scopes. D confuses memory footprint (largely arithmetic, hardware-independent) with wall-clock latency (kernel- and hardware-dependent). Memory savings do not automatically translate to speedup; a specific dequantized-GEMM kernel must exist for the target hardware, or the operation may run slower due to overhead.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: paper-scope discipline on model/task/calibration conditioning.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: latency depends on kernel availability, not just bit width.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: ablations isolate mechanism, not head-to-head verdicts.

assumptions: Familiarity with SmoothQuant, GPTQ, AWQ evaluation sections.
Distinction between memory footprint and wall-clock latency.
nonImplications: Does not imply the techniques never generalize; they often do, subject to re-evaluation.
Does not imply that ablations are useless — they characterize mechanism.

distractorRationales.D: Confuses memory footprint with latency speedup.
